Promoted city modules, PCG/PLA/HLOD outputs, Data Layer migrations, and imported environment packs require simple collision, authored fallback coverage, human-scale proportions, streaming budgets, and Mac package-smoke evidence before runtime scaling.

World Partition/Data Layer fallback station uses five small review cards, short labels, and local lights to expose state/time/mode tags without replacing the generated city or adding heavy streaming cost.

The narrative world-story deck uses five nonblocking story cards, a few cable markers, short labels, and local lights to expose the coding-rescues-people premise without increasing combat or save-system cost.
The canonical lore deck uses five lore cards, one backboard, and local lights to expose premise, pillars, factions, technology rules, and city chapter data without changing runtime systems.
Generated city output review lane must stay lightweight, nonblocking, deterministic by city seed, and promotion-gated before any Houdini/PCG cell replaces fallback runtime city geometry.
